title: Article 94 — Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker

content.overview: Article 94 provides that a member holding office as Speaker or Deputy Speaker of the House of the People vacates office if he ceases to be a member of the House, may resign by writing (Speaker to the Deputy Speaker; Deputy Speaker to the Speaker), and may be removed by a resolution of the House passed by a majority of all the then members of the House after at least fourteen days’ notice. The Speaker continues until immediately before the first meeting of the House after dissolution.
content.glance: Speaker/Deputy Speaker (LS): vacate if cease to be members; resign in writing; removable by majority of all then members after 14 days’ notice. Speaker continues till first meeting after dissolution.
content.study:
Article 94 parallels Article 90 for Lok Sabha officers. Special feature: the Speaker does not vacate office on dissolution of the House but continues until immediately before the first meeting of the House after dissolution.

Examination: cessation; resignation addresses; removal majority + notice; Speaker’s continuity after dissolution.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Vacates on ceasing to be a member (with Speaker continuity until first meeting after dissolution).
2. Resignation in writing (Speaker→Deputy Speaker; Deputy Speaker→Speaker).
3. Removal: resolution by majority of all then members after ≥14 days’ notice.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How is the Speaker of the Lok Sabha removed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 94, the Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then members of the House, after at least fourteen days’ notice of the intention to move the resolution.

examTips: Removal: majority of all then members + 14 days’ notice; Speaker continues after dissolution until next first meeting.

keyTakeaways: Art 94: Speaker/Deputy Speaker vacation, resignation, removal; Speaker continuity after dissolution.
